Author: @PaulLoh
Content: Normally I'm a sushi guy and don't like my fish cooked. Actually, the only fish that I enjoy cooked is sea bass. But one day, I was in an experimental mood. I had a catfish and I didn't know how to cook it properly. So I grabbed my gallon jug of soy sauce. I put the fish whole into my rice cooker and filled the machine with soy sauce, completely immersing the fish. I just set it to a regular rice cooking cycle and trusted the process. When the machine beeped, I took the fish out. Let me tell you, it was the best cooked fish I have ever had. The soy sauce soaked into every fiber of the catfish and flavored it, but it was also the best texture. So juicy and tender, and not overly salty tasting. If you try this experiment, I know you will not regret it.

Author: @xorngoh7303
Content:
Seeing how Guga massacred the grouper was painful to watch as a Chinese. For a fresh good fish like grouper, you don't dry age it or soak it in soy sauce. You steam it. Add ginger slices, tomato slices, light soy sauce, rice wine or mirin, some slices of salted vegetable and pickled plums, some slices of shiitake mushroom, some cubes of silken tofu, then finally a tiny bit of water. Then you steam it over water for about 10 minutes. About 3 minutes before it is fully cooked, you then drizzle some oil on the fish and then add some slices of chili, some green onion strips, even some coriander/cilantro (don't cut it or anything just put a few whole leaves and stalks in), and then you steam it some more until it is fully cooked. This is called Teochew steamed fish. It allows you to taste the natural freshness of the fish, with hints of saltiness and sourness.
Some foods have a very strong taste and taste delicious, but you soon get overpowered and tired or sick of the taste after several bites. Like your body just rejects it and you can't seem to make yourself take another bite. But for this fish, you wouldn't get tired of the taste because it is light and fresh tasting. You can eat the whole fish without that overpowering or getting sick or tired of the taste feeling. This is not a dish that is meant to blow your mind with flavours but rather a dish that make you want to keep eating more. I usually dislike eating fish due to being lazy and getting annoyed at picking out the bones, but for this fish I can eat the whole fish. If you don't want to pick out bones from the fish, you can simply use fish fillet that has no bones because it works too.

Author: @naitsirkxify
Content:
This is how a lot of Filipinos soak their fish, mostly milkfish:
1 part soy sauce
1 part cane vinegar (maybe less, depends how you sour you like it)
1 part Sprite/7up
a gazillion Asian amount of  crushed garlic, typically around 5 to 7 heads of garlic per 1 liter of soy sauce
2 large red onions chopped or minced
50-100 grams of crushed peppercorn per 1 liter of soy sauce

Soak the fish for 1 week.

@GugaFoods, I dare you make this with cod, grouper or any white meat fish. This is actually somewhat a daily recipe for us here in the Philippines.
